item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J01255","case1_error":"Applies only two halvings over 30 years, incorrectly assigning the first halving to age 20.","case2_error":"Adds one boxcar’s capacity per color without multiplying by the number of boxcars of each color.","reason":"The first omits a sequential halving; the second omits multiplicities when aggregating capacities.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01256","case1_error":"Treats each two-dozen set as 12 cups, omitting the factor of two.","case2_error":"Derives 14 correctly but asserts an unsupported 26 in the final sentence as well as the leading marker.","reason":"The first misrepresents the quantity per set; the second supplies a contradictory final number after correct calculations.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01257","case1_error":"Reduces the required rope length by 25% instead of accounting for reduced usable length of purchased rope.","case2_error":"Uses the 10% discount amount as the boots’ purchase price instead of subtracting it from $110.","reason":"The first applies loss to the required quantity in the wrong direction; the second confuses the discount amount with the remaining price.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01258","case1_error":"Reverses the twice-as-many relationship, multiplying Emmy’s remaining eight by two instead of dividing.","case2_error":"No clear error: 'one-quarter more' gives 8 + 2 + 7 = 17.","reason":"The second solution correctly follows the question; the reference omits the base quantity implied by 'more.'","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J01259","case1_error":"Charges for only one sandwich and evaluates the displayed sum as $30.25 instead of $32.25.","case2_error":"Subtracts one bun per excluded guest instead of three, producing 28 rather than 24 buns.","reason":"Both mishandle multiplicity, but the first also makes an explicit numerical evaluation error; their complete observable error mechanisms differ.","judgment":"different"}]}
